propositions: A leaked 0-byte enrich-drain.lock file with no owner stamp wedges enrichment permanently, returning {"skipped": "lock-held"} at INFO level and silently halting processing with no error signal.

The drain lock lacks ownership discipline: _acquire_advisory_lock creates O_EXCL but never writes a stamp to the fd, and a drainer killed between acquire and release leaves an unstamped orphan that every subsequent drain refuses without staleness adjudication.

Extraction of the decision table from _mkdir_lock_is_stale into a shared _stamp_is_stale core, with an unrecognised_via_ceiling parameter, allows non-v2 (unstamped) drain locks to fall through to the wall-clock ceiling while preserving mkdir's legacy routing.

Drain lock reclaim on FileExistsError consults stamped_file_is_stale with at most one bounded retry, then logs WARNING naming holder and age; drain() skip logs also move to WARNING with holder attribution.
Doctor's drain leg now decodes the v2 stamp and reports a real staleness verdict (stale-lock finding at exit 1 for dead holder, no finding at exit 0 for live holder) instead of not-assessable.
